page.layout: One printed page (p. 168), set in two columns of running text with marginal notes in the left margin. The right edge of the neighbouring page shows as a narrow strip at the far right and is not transcribed. Full-width text runs from the top of the page to the catchword at the foot.

main_text.l: Israelitico permisit uxorum repudia : eo consilio, u-
ti exponit optimus Legis interpres Christus, ne ex
{1}duritiâ cordis humani & effræni maritorum in
conjuges asperitate & sævitiâ graviora pullulá-
rent incommoda. Dico tertiò, ejusmodi tamen
lege neminem {2}obligari ad faciendum id quod
Lex permittit : Finis enim permissionis est, non ut
id fiat quod lege permittitur, sed ne ultra id quod
leges permittunt fiat. Proinde, sicut permissio ipsa
negativa tantùm est, ita obligationem inducit non
nisi negativam : hoc est, obligatur subditus, si ipsi
libuerit facere quod Lex permittit, præstitutos sibi
à lege fines non excedere. Dico quartò, permissionem
mali positivam, si plura aut graviora sint mala
quæ ex ejusmodi permissione consequuntur, quàm sunt
ea in quorum remedium adhiberi prætenditur, ut
plerumque fit, non esse licitam : præsertim si per-
missioni rei turpis accedat, ex impolito tributo,
turpis etiam lucri suspicio. Dico quintò, neminem
obligari tali lege ad faciendum id quòd permitti-
tur ; imò aliunde obligari unumquemque, non
obstante legis permissione, ad id non faciendum.
Ratio est ; Quoad priorem partem, quia est con-
tra naturam permissionis, ut sit obligatoria : cùm
permissio det libertatem, & omnis obligatio sit vin-
culum quoddam. Quoad posteriorem partem, quia
supponimus id quod lege humanâ sic permittitur
esse ex se malum ; & lege Dei obligamur ad non
faciendum malum. Permissio itaque mali, quate-

l.i: nus nuda permissio est, neminem obligat ad facien-

main_text.l: dum ; quatenus autem mali permissio est, unum-
quemque obligat ad non faciendum id quod per-
mittitur.
XX. Atqui dictum est jam ante sæpius, omni
Legi adesse vim obligativam, quæ eam ita indivi-
duè comitatur, ut posità Lege necesse sit sequi ob-
ligationem & obligatione sublatâ unà tolli & Legem.

page.notes: The right-hand strip is the edge of the neighbouring page and is left out. Marks {1} and {2} stand in the text; their matching notes are not clearly visible on the scan. The left margin notes "3.", "5.", and "* Mat. 19. 8." were placed beside their lines. The margin note "* Aliud est indulgere, aliud jubere. Tert. de Monog. c 14." (the Tertullian reference) stands in the left margin beside "lege neminem" and is not reproduced here because the scan is too faint to confirm its position and wording with certainty. The margin number "4." stands beside "Dico quartò" and is copied as a note. The catchword "gem." is the start of "Legem" printed below the last line. The word "positivam" is printed with a long s and read as such. Some italic and roman distinctions are uncertain at the scan resolution.
